title: Zoom Pricing in 2026: Plans, Add-Ons and Costs
summary: Zoom pricing offers five plans from Basic to Enterprise, charged per user with available add-ons. Determine which tier best fits your needs and budget.
body_markdown:
## Automating Zoom registrations and recordings with Activepieces


If you already pay for Zoom, Activepieces can make the plan work harder.


It is a workflow automation tool with a Zoom integration listed in its docs, one of 746 integrations in an MIT-licensed core, and its free plan allows unlimited flows with 1,000 credits a month.


It can move registrants into your CRM, recordings into shared storage and summaries into chat, so the plan you bought gets used with less manual work. Think of each automated step as one run you no longer do by hand, and count it that way.


### Registrants to CRM


Every Zoom registration is a lead sitting in the wrong system. A flow can start on a new registrant and write that person into your CRM, the database your sales or community team works from.


The consequence is practical: nobody exports a spreadsheet after each webinar, and follow-up starts from the record rather than from whoever remembered to upload the list.


### Saving Zoom recordings to shared storage


If a recording lives only in an organizer's Zoom account, the rest of the team can't find it. A flow can trigger when a recording finishes and copy it to the shared drive your team already searches.


Add AI steps and the same flow can draft a summary from the transcript and post it to a team chat channel.


The screenshot below shows that pattern in a different job. It's a content workflow where a trigger feeds two OpenAI steps, and the selected WordPress step fills its Title and Content fields with references to their output.


The point to take is that each step reads the one before it, with no copying between them.


Swap the last step for a storage or chat action and you have the recording flow.


### What automation doesn't change on Zoom bills


None of this lowers your Zoom bill. Seats, plan and add-ons are still set by meeting length and headcount, and automation sits on top of that invoice. It saves labor, not licenses, and the automation tool has its own usage to price before you commit.
